chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū ʿAlī, the companion of al-Anmāṭ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام or Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
“The adhān is given for al-ẓuhr at six rakʿahs, and the adhān is given for al-ʿaṣr at six rakʿahs after al-ẓuhr.”

key_terms.يُؤَذَّنُ: the adhān is proclaimed or called

ai.seo_question: When should the adhān for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr be called according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a ruling concerning the timing of the adhān for the ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers in relation to six rakʿahs. It reflects a jurisprudential teaching on the prayer schedule and the announced commencement of these salat times.
